crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Fabricated citations and fact checking sit in research integrity and AI governance. They cover references that are invented, incomplete, or attached to claims they do not support, and the checks that catch them. The problem grows when language models draft literature reviews or summaries because fluent text can carry plausible but nonexistent sources. Fact checking here means tracing a claim back to the original paper, dataset, or record and confirming what it actually says. This topic matters to researchers, editors, reviewers, and anyone using AI to assemble evidence.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Fact checking runs on access to primary sources: publisher pages, DOI records, preprint servers, library catalogues, and institutional repositories. Reference managers, citation databases, and full text search help locate a paper, but the decisive step is opening the source and reading the relevant passage. AI tools can speed screening and claim extraction, yet they depend on the same underlying corpus and can reproduce the same gaps. On this site, the library holds 135 research papers and 12646 claims extracted from research works, which gives a bounded set for checking.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical check starts with a citation or claim, then verifies that the cited work exists, that the authors and title match, and that the passage supports the statement. Reviewers may compare the claim against the abstract, methods, results, and limitations, not just the title. Automated systems can flag suspicious references by checking metadata, DOI resolution, and citation context, but human judgment decides whether a mismatch is an error, a paraphrase, or a fabrication. On this site, links go to the original paper rather than to a secondary search tool, so the reader can inspect the source directly.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Fabricated citations damage trust, waste reviewer time, and can spread into policy, technical, or public decisions if left unchecked. Provenance matters: a claim should carry a traceable path to the exact source, version, and passage. Institutions and journals set authorship, disclosure, and correction policies, and some have retraction or integrity processes for fabricated references. Policies often require disclosure of AI assistance, and citations are expected to be verified before publication.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Fact checking is moving toward tighter integration with reference managers, publisher workflows, and claim level databases. Better tooling may detect fabricated citations at submission, but generated text will also become more fluent and harder to spot by style alone. A durable response is provenance by design: persistent identifiers, versioned sources, and links that resolve to the original paper. As AI systems take on more literature synthesis, research integrity will depend on checks that are routine, auditable, and independent of the tool that produced the draft.
